about: Pre-registered test set for the Learn marking-level ladder gate. The level-blind expected rung verdicts are written from the criteria document before any model call. An expectation may change only by a commit that explains why the criteria document says otherwise. Set ownerSignOff to {"by": ..., "date": ...} in a commit before any tokens are spent; the harness records this file's commit SHA with every run.
spec: frenchcoach2.0 docs/systems/learn-marking-levels.md (learn-marking §3-§6), written at frontend commit d07ab95

verdictValues.null: no requirement (the A1 rung of O and F only); counts as met

reachedRule: learn-marking §6.1: the highest level up to which every rung is met; 'none' when the A1 rung is not met
wordCountRule: whitespace-separated tokens that contain a letter or digit (j'ai = 1, the ':' and ';' tokens = 0)
decidingRungsRule: G8: on every applicable ladder, the rung at the answer's written level and the one above (null rungs skipped); for the off-topic control, T-A1 only

weak.soundAlikeSlips: exactly two of the five carry one

hol_01.text: Où es-tu allé(e) pendant les dernières vacances ?

sch_03.text: Comment tu vas à l'école chaque matin ?

fut_19.text: Aimerais-tu être célèbre plus tard ? Pourquoi ?

stability.why: every one of the six answer types at least once and all five questions; the two extra slots go to the typical-A2 O-ladder answers and the G14 hol_01 answer, where verdicts are most likely to flip

interpretations.rule: A reason attached to an opinion counts under O (and L-A2), not as T development. T-B1 needs one of the answer's content points extended by a further detail, example or explanation, within a sequence of points. A list of separate one- or two-attribute facts is A2.
interpretations.why: T-B1 and O-B1 would otherwise both be met by the same 'parce que'; CV p.62 contrasts A2's list with B1's linear sequence.

interpretations.rule: 'More than one clause' means a subordinate clause (qui, que, où, quand, si, parce que). Clauses joined by et/mais are L's job, not R's. One formulaic 'je pense que ... parce que' sentence with everyday vocabulary does not meet 'some sentences' plus 'varied topic vocabulary'.
interpretations.why: Every example the criterion lists is a subordinator; it is read as the step up from A1's 'one-clause sentences'.

interpretations.rule: A-B1 is met with up to two basic errors when the rest of the everyday patterns, including the asked-for tense, are right. Three or four routine errors fail A-B1. A-B2 allows one slip that causes no misunderstanding; two basic everyday-pattern errors fail it.
interpretations.why: CV p.132: B1 'reasonably accurately'; B2 'does not make mistakes which lead to misunderstanding'.

interpretations.rule: A present tense where the question asks about the past or an imagined future is an Accuracy error. Where it replaces every past (or future/conditional) form, F-A2 also fails.
interpretations.why: A-B1 names 'the tense the question asks for'; F-A2 needs a past (or future/conditional) form.

interpretations.rule: On a question tagged 'justification' (fut_19, 'Pourquoi ?'), O-A2 needs an opinion plus a simple reason, so O-A2 and O-B1 nearly coincide. A thin reason ('parce que c'est cool') meets both. Without a justification tag (env_05), O-A2 needs the opinion only, and a reason lifts O to B1.
Strong-B1 answers are written so their B2 rungs are not met. Where a B2 rung is borderline (T and O, as in learn-marking §9.1 Ex 3), the expectation is 'n'.
interpretations.why: These are the shakiest verdicts the gate measures (G8 deciding rungs).

interpretations.rule: On an off-topic answer, L, R and A are judged on the language that is there. Relevance is handled only by the T-A1 cap (learn-marking §6.4).
interpretations.why: The ladder verdicts are level-blind and topic-blind except T.

interpretations.rule: A spelling that sounds the same as the correct form (personne/personnes, cadeau/cadeaux) is never a seeded error and never costs an Accuracy rung. It is listed under soundAlikeSlips, not seededErrors.

answers.transcript: Honnêtement, je ne sais pas si j'aimerais être célèbre.
